data.name: Yamini
data.gender_notes: Yamini is used as a female name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit yāminī, 'night', from the root yam, 'to restrain'. Its root is Sanskrit yam (यम्). A classical Sanskrit term for night. Yamini is a Sanskrit name meaning “Night; the night goddess”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Yamini expresses “Night; the night goddess”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.etymology: From the Sanskrit yāminī, 'night', from the root yam, 'to restrain'.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Yamini total 35, reducing to 8. Number 8 is associated with ambition, authority and material mastery.

vedic_reference.note: Yamini is a name mentioned in various Hindu scriptures and is associated with the god of death, Yama. The name Yami is derived from the Sanskrit word yama, which means 'god of death'. Yami is also referred to as the goddess of death and is often depicted as a beautiful and terrifying figure who is responsible for taking the souls of the deceased to the underworld.
